page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.24xlarge is a Gen9 compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom 64-bit ARM-based AWS Graviton processors. It provides 96 dedicated physical CPU cores without hyperthreading, operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The server contains 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core typical of compute-intensive cloud infrastructure.

The instance comes equipped with 5,700 GB of directly attached local NVMe SSD instance storage for high-speed local data access. Baseline network connectivity is delivered at 50 Gbps. Built on the ARM64 architecture, the server omits x86 vector instructions such as AVX or AVX-512, requiring application binaries compiled specifically for 64-bit ARM environments.

By combining high-density Graviton cores with integrated NVMe SSD instance store volumes, the server offers strong compute density and qualitative I/O resource efficiency per node. The primary tradeoff lies in the ephemeral nature of local instance store volumes, which require application-level replication or external storage for persistent state. This configuration is suited for compute-heavy workloads needing rapid local scratch space, including high-throughput data processing pipelines, distributed databases, batch analytics, and continuous integration builds.
description: Amazon Web Services c9gd.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by 96 dedicated 64-bit ARM-based AWS Graviton cores operating at 3.3 GHz. Configured on the AWS Nitro system, it features 192.0 GB of RAM alongside 5,700 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage and 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio delivers high computational density per core, while integrated NVMe storage accommodates data-intensive local operations. Because the physical architecture relies on ARM64 processors without x86 instruction extensions, software must be compiled for ARM. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage provides strong qualitative efficiency for I/O-heavy computing without relying entirely on external EBS volumes, though local data remains ephemeral. This server is suited for heavy batch processing, high-throughput distributed databases, continuous integration, and data analytics.
